rationale: The bank's policy correctly mandates that the KYC policy comprising the four key elements must be approved by the Board of Directors or a delegated committee, which matches the RBI requirement.

evidence.quote: (1) The bank shall have a KYC policy. The Board of Directors of the bank, or any committee to which the Board has delegated power, shall duly approve the KYC policy.

(2) The KYC policy shall include following four key elements:
(i) Customer Acceptance Policy;
(ii) Risk Management
(iii) Customer Identification Procedures (CIP); and
(iv) Monitoring of Transactions

arguments.query: This Policy, comprising the Customer Acceptance Policy, Risk Management, Customer Identification Procedures and Monitoring of Transactions, shall be approved by the Board of Directors or by a committee to which the Board has delegated this power.

rationale: The bank policy states that the ML/TF risk assessment shall be carried out at least once every two years, whereas RBI directions mandate that the bank shall review it at least annually.

evidence.quote: However, the bank shall review it at least annually.

arguments.query: The money laundering and terrorist financing risk assessment shall be carried out at a periodicity decided by the Board, and in any case at least once every two years.

rationale: The bank's policy allows rejecting onboarding or periodic updation without qualification, whereas RBI mandates that the bank shall not reject an application for onboarding or periodic updation of KYC without application of mind and that reasons must be recorded.

evidence.quote: The bank shall not reject an application for onboarding or periodic updation of KYC without application of mind. The officer concerned shall duly record the reason(s) for rejection.

arguments.query: A branch may reject an application for onboarding or periodic updation of KYC where the customer does not furnish the documents within the stipulated time.

rationale: The bank policy sets the threshold for a company's beneficial owner at more than 25 percent, whereas the current RBI Commercial Banks KYC Directions require it to be more than 10 percent.

evidence.quote: 'Controlling ownership interest' means ownership of / entitlement to more than 10 percent of the shares or capital or profits of the company.

arguments.query: For a company, the beneficial owner shall be the natural person who, alone or together, owns or is entitled to more than 25 per cent of the shares, capital or profits of the company, or who exercises control.

rationale: The policy permits term loans up to Rs. 50,000, but RBI directions mandate that the aggregate amount of term loans sanctioned shall not exceed ₹60,000 in a year for such accounts (a weaker/incorrect limit or incorrect standard compared to the mandated Rs 60,000 figure).

evidence.quote: As regards borrowal accounts, the bank shall sanction only term loans. The aggregate amount of term loans sanctioned shall not exceed ₹60,000 in a year.

arguments.query: Accounts opened in non-face-to-face mode using Aadhaar OTP-based e-KYC shall have an aggregate deposit balance of not more than Rs. 1 lakh and aggregate credits of not more than Rs. 2 lakh in a financial year, and term loans sanctioned in such accounts shall not exceed Rs. 50,000 in a year.

rationale: The policy clause correctly mandates that accounts opened through V-CIP are made operational only after being subject to concurrent audit, matching the RBI requirement.

evidence.quote: All accounts opened through V-CIP shall be made operational only after being subject to concurrent audit, to ensure the integrity of process and its acceptability of the outcome.

notes: cited notification(s) marked as replaced: rbi-11566

arguments.query: Accounts opened through the Video-based Customer Identification Process (V-CIP) shall be made operational only after the account has been subjected to concurrent audit.

rationale: The bank's policy to review risk categorization at the time of periodic KYC updation complies with the risk-based approach for periodic KYC updation under the RBI Directions.

evidence.quote: The bank shall carry out periodic updation at least once in every two years for high-risk customers, once in every eight years for medium risk customers and once in every 10 years for low-risk customers from the date of opening of the account / last KYC updation.

arguments.query: The risk categorisation of customer accounts shall be reviewed at the time of periodic updation of KYC.

rationale: The clause matches the exact periodic KYC updation timelines mandated for high, medium, and low-risk customers under RBI commercial bank directions.

evidence.quote: However, the bank shall carry out periodic updation at least once in every two years for high-risk customers, once in every eight years for medium risk customers and once in every 10 years for low-risk customers from the date of opening of the account / last KYC updation.

arguments.query: Periodic updation of KYC shall be carried out at least once every two years for high-risk customers, once every eight years for medium-risk customers and once every ten years for low-risk customers, from the date of opening of the account or the last KYC updation.

rationale: The bank's clause states it will send at least three advance intimations, but omits the mandatory requirement from the RBI notification that at least one of these advance intimations must be sent by letter.

evidence.quote: Prior to the due date of periodic updation of KYC, the bank shall give at least three advance intimations, including at least one intimation by letter, at appropriate intervals to its customers through available communication options / channels for complying with the requirement of periodic updation of KYC.

arguments.query: Before the due date for periodic updation of KYC, the Bank shall send the customer at least three advance intimations through the available communication channels.

rationale: The RBI directions require senior management's approval to continue the business relationship when an existing customer becomes a PEP, whereas the policy incorrectly permits it with the approval of the Branch Manager.

evidence.quote: in the event of an existing customer or the beneficial owner of an existing account subsequently becoming a PEP, the bank obtains the senior management's approval to continue the business relationship;
in the event of an existing customer or the beneficial owner of an existing account subsequently becoming a PEP, senior management's approval is obtained to continue the business relationship;

arguments.query: Where an existing customer, or the beneficial owner of an existing account, subsequently becomes a politically exposed person, the business relationship may continue with the approval of the Branch Manager.

rationale: The bank's policy preserves transaction records for ten years and identification records for five years after the relationship ends, which exceeds or meets the minimum retention periods required by RBI directions.

evidence.quote: maintain all necessary records of transactions between the bank and the customer, both domestic and international, for at least five years from the date of transaction;

preserve the records pertaining to the identification of the customers and their addresses, obtained while opening the account and during the course of business relationship, for at least five years after the business relationship has ended;

arguments.query: Records of transactions shall be preserved for at least ten years from the date of the transaction, and records of customer identification and address for at least five years after the business relationship has ended.

rationale: The bank policy allows 30 days to upload KYC records to CKYCR, whereas RBI directions mandate uploading within 10 days of the commencement of an account-based relationship.

evidence.quote: In terms of provision of Rule 9(1A) of the PML Rules, the bank shall capture customer's KYC records and upload onto CKYCR within 10 days of commencement of an account-based relationship with the customer.

arguments.query: The KYC records of new customers shall be uploaded to the Central KYC Records Registry within 30 days of the commencement of the account-based relationship.

rationale: The provided RBI Commercial Banks KYC Directions do not contain specific rules regulating adverse media screening requirements at onboarding or on an annual basis.

arguments.query: All customers shall be screened against adverse media sources at onboarding and at least once a year thereafter.

rationale: The clause deals with internal administrative meetings and scheduling for the Compliance Department, which is an internal matter not governed by RBI regulations.

arguments.query: The Compliance Department shall hold its weekly coordination meeting every Monday at 10 a.m.

rationale: The clause correctly includes the requirement to seek OTP-based consent for credit cards not activated within 30 days, but omits the mandatory requirement to close the credit card account without cost to the customer within seven working days if no consent is received.

evidence.quote: If no consent is received for activating the card, card-issuers shall close the credit card account without any cost to the customer within seven working days from date of seeking confirmation from the customer.

arguments.query: Where a credit card has not been activated by the customer within 30 days of issue, the Bank shall seek One Time Password based consent from the cardholder for activating it.

rationale: The RBI notification requires the penalty to be calculated per calendar day of delay, whereas the policy states it is payable for each working day of delay, which creates a conflict by using a weaker standard.

evidence.quote: Failure on the part of the card-issuers to complete the process of closure within seven working days shall result in a penalty of ₹500 per calendar day of delay payable to the cardholder, till the closure of the account provided there is no outstanding in the account.

arguments.query: A request to close a credit card shall be completed within seven working days, subject to payment of all dues; for any delay, the Bank shall pay the cardholder Rs. 500 for each working day of delay.

rationale: The policy correctly aligns with RBI instructions requiring credit card accounts to be reported as past due and late payment charges levied only when past due for more than three days.

evidence.quote: Card-issuers shall report a credit card account as 'past due' to credit information companies (CICs) or levy penal charges, viz. late payment charges and other related charges, if any, only when a credit card account remains 'past due' for more than three days.

arguments.query: A credit card account shall be reported as past due to credit information companies, and late payment charges levied, only when the account remains past due for more than three days.

rationale: The policy mandates obtaining explicit prior consent for renewed credit cards, whereas the RBI regulation requires providing an option to decline before dispatching the renewed card, omitting the specific mandatory element of the decline option mechanism.

evidence.quote: 71. A card-issuer shall not dispatch a card to a customer unsolicited. In case of renewal of an existing card, the cardholder shall be provided an option to decline the same if he / she wants to do so before dispatching the renewed card.

arguments.query: Renewed credit cards shall be dispatched only after obtaining the cardholder's explicit prior consent.

rationale: No relevant RBI notification governing the closure and transfer of recurring deposit accounts upon missed instalments was found in the provided passages.

arguments.query: Recurring deposit accounts with three consecutive missed monthly instalments shall be closed and the balance transferred to the depositor's savings account.

rationale: The bank's policy permits issuing debit cards on cash credit accounts, which directly contradicts RBI directions prohibiting the issuance of debit cards to cash credit or loan accounts.

evidence.quote: Debit cards shall only be issued to customers having Savings Bank / Current Accounts.
The bank shall not issue debit cards to cash credit / loan accounts.

arguments.query: Debit cards may be issued on savings bank accounts, current accounts and cash credit accounts.

rationale: The policy defines bulk deposits as Rs. 2 crore and above, whereas the current Master Direction for Scheduled Commercial Banks defines bulk deposits as single Rupee term deposits of Rupees three crore and above.

evidence.quote: 4.3.1 Single Rupee term deposits of Rupees three crore and above for Scheduled Commercial Banks (excluding RRBs) and SFBs.

arguments.query: Differential interest rates may be offered on bulk deposits, that is, single rupee term deposits of Rs. 2 crore and above.

rationale: The policy mandates half-yearly interest crediting on savings deposits, whereas RBI directions require banks to credit interest at quarterly or shorter intervals.

evidence.quote: Interest on savings deposit shall be credited by a bank at quarterly or shorter intervals.

arguments.query: Interest on savings deposits shall be credited at half-yearly intervals.

rationale: The clause states that interest rates for bulk deposits shall be disclosed in advance on the bank's website, but omits the mandatory timing requirement to disclose them at 10:00 am with a grace time of 10 minutes, latest by 10:10 am, on each business day.

evidence.quote: However, interest rates payable on bulk deposits shall be disclosed on the bank's website at 10:00 am with a grace time of 10 minutes, latest by 10:10 am, on each business day.

arguments.query: Interest rates payable on bulk deposits shall be disclosed in advance on the Bank's website.

rationale: The bank's policy correctly mirrors the RBI requirement that unclaimed proceeds of a matured term deposit shall earn interest at the savings account rate or the contracted rate, whichever is lower.

evidence.quote: If a Term Deposit (TD) matures and proceeds are unpaid, the amount left unclaimed with a bank, shall attract rate of interest as applicable to savings account or the contracted rate of interest on the matured TD, whichever is lower.

arguments.query: Unclaimed proceeds of a matured term deposit shall earn interest at the savings account rate or the contracted rate on the matured deposit, whichever is lower.

rationale: The bank's policy correctly mandates processing inoperative account activation requests within three working days of receiving the complete application, matching RBI requirements.

evidence.quote: The bank shall process requests for activation of inoperative account / unclaimed deposits within three working days from the receipt of the complete application.
The banks shall process requests for activation of inoperative account/ unclaimed deposits within three working days from the receipt of the complete application.

arguments.query: Requests to activate an inoperative account shall be processed within three working days of receipt of the complete application.

rationale: The clause pertains to celebrating an internal foundation day for the Cards business unit, which is an internal matter not governed by any RBI regulations.

arguments.query: The Cards business unit shall celebrate its foundation day on 1 July each year.
